C0.content: What is the boiling point of water at sea level, in degrees Celsius?

Water boils at **100°C** (212°F) at sea level, which corresponds to standard atmospheric pressure of 1 atmosphere (101.325 kPa).

Note that this boiling point decreases at higher altitudes due to lower atmospheric pressure—for example, water boils at around 93-94°C at an altitude of about 2,000 meters.
